turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Morning, Alex. Got a sec? I need to vent about the deploy last night.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Sure, what happened? I saw the alert for the checkout service.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, that was mine. I provisioned the new instances for the sale traffic, but I didn't set up autoscaling. Thought the fixed pool would be enough.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Ouch. So when the spike hit...

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Service went down hard. And because the checkout API is called by the cart and order services, the downtime cascaded to them too. Total mess.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That's rough. But at least you know the fix now, right?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, I've already enabled autoscaling on the instances. Should handle the next spike better.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Hey, I saw the load test results from this morning. Looked good?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Actually, yes! The autoscaling kicked in and the service absorbed the traffic spike without a blip. I'm pretty happy about that.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Nice. But I also noticed you pushed a change to the API yesterday. Something about pagination?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Oh, that. I shipped the API without pagination originally — my bad. Under load, the endpoint timed out because it was returning thousands of rows at once.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Classic. So you added pagination?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yep, added it over the weekend. And in the load test, the API held up under heavy load — no timeouts, response times stable.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Great. So we're solid now?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I think so. Autoscaling plus pagination should cover us.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: Hey, I heard there was another incident last night. What happened?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah... so, remember I enabled autoscaling on the instances? Turns out that wasn't enough.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: What do you mean? It worked in the load test.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: In the load test, yes. But in production, the spike was sharper and the autoscaling lagged. The service went down again, and the dependent services started failing too.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: So the cascade happened again?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. I was wrong about autoscaling being the silver bullet. It helps, but it doesn't stop the cascading failures when the downstream calls just hang.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: So what did you do?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I replaced the autoscaling-only approach with circuit breakers on all dependent calls. Now if the checkout service is slow or down, the cart and order services fail gracefully instead of timing out and dragging everything down.

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.text: That makes sense. So autoscaling is still there, but the circuit breakers are the real safety net?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. Autoscaling alone fell short — the circuit breakers are what actually stop the cascade. Lesson learned.
